PORTSIDE — A fire tore through a storage warehouse at the Portside Cannery late Thursday night, causing what officials estimate could be more than $2 million in damage, though no injuries were reported.

The fire was first reported at 11:42 p.m. by a security guard who noticed smoke near the loading dock on the building's east side. More than 40 firefighters from three surrounding districts responded, and the blaze was brought under control by 3:15 a.m. Friday, according to Fire Chief Mara Oduya.

“At this point we have no reason to believe this was arson,” Oduya said at a morning briefing. “Investigators are looking closely at an electrical panel near where the fire appears to have started, but it's too early to name a definitive cause.”

The cannery, which employs about 120 workers, was closed for the overnight shift when the fire broke out, and plant manager Devon Track said all staff were accounted for. Production is expected to resume within the week once inspectors clear the undamaged sections of the plant.

The warehouse sits adjacent to a seafood storage facility operated by Bayline Seafood, a separate company that leases space in the same industrial park. Bayline said its facility sustained only minor smoke damage and remained operational Friday morning.

Thursday's fire is the second at the industrial park in two years; a 2024 blaze destroyed a textile warehouse two lots away, a fire that investigators later attributed to a faulty forklift battery charger. Chief Oduya said there is no indication the two incidents are related.

Local business owners near the industrial park said they were relieved the fire did not spread further. “We could see the glow from three blocks away,” said Priya Nandan, who owns a diner across the street and stayed open through the night to give firefighters coffee.

The Portside Fire Department said a full incident report would be released within 30 days, standard for fires of this size, and that the state fire marshal's office has been notified given the estimated dollar value of the damage, though such notification does not by itself indicate any suspicion of wrongdoing.

The Portside City Council, which oversees fire-code inspections for the industrial park, confirmed the park had passed its most recent inspection in March and said it had no immediate plans to order additional inspections of the remaining tenants. Chief Oduya added that residents within a two-block radius reported no smoke-related health complaints as of Friday morning.

Portside Cannery's parent company, Coastal Provisions Inc., said in a statement that it carries insurance covering both property damage and business interruption, and that it does not expect the fire to affect its ability to fulfill existing orders.

state: Preliminary Results of a Phase II Trial of Odarafenib in Advanced Melanoma. In this open-label Phase II trial, 84 patients with unresectable stage III or IV melanoma received odarafenib 200 mg twice daily. At a median follow-up of 11 months, the objective response rate was 34% (95% CI, 24–45%), and median progression-free survival was 7.2 months. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 18% of patients, most commonly rash and elevated liver enzymes; no treatment-related deaths were observed. These preliminary findings suggest odarafenib may offer clinical benefit in this population, but the authors caution that confirmatory Phase III data are needed before any conclusions about survival benefit can be drawn. Eligible patients had an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1 and had received at most one prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; patients with active brain metastases were excluded. Dose reductions for adverse events were permitted per protocol, and 22% of patients required at least one dose reduction. A data safety monitoring board reviewed toxicity data at each 20-patient enrollment milestone and did not recommend early stopping of the trial.

Technical Report: Evaluating FalconNet and OrcaNet on the MERIT Benchmark.

We evaluate two recent vision-language models, FalconNet-7B and OrcaNet-13B, on the MERIT benchmark, a suite of eight tasks spanning visual question answering, chart reasoning, and document understanding. All models are evaluated zero-shot, with no task-specific fine-tuning.

On the aggregate MERIT score, OrcaNet-13B achieves 61.4 points, compared to 58.9 for FalconNet-7B. However, the gap is not uniform across tasks. On the chart-reasoning subset, FalconNet-7B scores 52.3, outperforming OrcaNet-13B's 49.1, which we attribute to FalconNet's dedicated chart-pretraining stage. On document understanding, OrcaNet-13B leads by a wider margin, 71.0 versus 60.7.

We also compare inference latency: FalconNet-7B, being roughly half the parameter count, runs at 340 ms per query on our reference A100 setup, versus 610 ms for OrcaNet-13B.

For context, we note that a third model, PelicanVL-3B, was evaluated in a prior study (Ibarra et al., 2025) on a different, non-public benchmark, and is not directly comparable to the results here; we do not evaluate PelicanVL-3B in this work.

Both models show substantial weaknesses on the spatial-reasoning subset, scoring below 40 points, which we interpret as evidence that neither architecture has solved fine-grained spatial grounding. We caution that our results are based on a single evaluation run per model and may not capture the full variance of these benchmarks; a more thorough study with multiple seeds is left to future work.

Overall, these preliminary results suggest OrcaNet-13B may be preferable for document-heavy applications, while FalconNet-7B's lower latency and competitive chart-reasoning performance could make it attractive for latency-sensitive deployments.

The MERIT benchmark's eight tasks are drawn from a mix of publicly released datasets and a held-out set of 1,200 newly collected question-answer pairs designed to reduce the risk of training-data contamination. Each task contributes equally to the aggregate score regardless of the number of examples it contains.

A qualitative error analysis of 50 randomly sampled failures from each model suggests that FalconNet-7B's errors on document-understanding tasks are concentrated in multi-column layouts and dense tables, while OrcaNet-13B's chart-reasoning errors more often involve misreading axis labels rather than misunderstanding the underlying trend. We did not perform a similar qualitative analysis for the spatial-reasoning subset, which we leave to future work alongside the multi-seed evaluation. All code and evaluation prompts used in this report are being prepared for release alongside the camera-ready version of the paper.

state: A survey of the dwarf galaxy NGC 5253-B using the Alden Radio Array has detected an unusual radio pulse train recurring every 4.6 hours, a pattern the authors say may indicate a previously uncatalogued magnetar, though they note that instrumental artifacts have not been fully ruled out. Follow-up observations are scheduled for early next year to confirm the periodicity and rule out terrestrial interference. The authors emphasize that, unlike the well-studied repeating fast radio bursts from galaxy FRB-catalog source J0157+43, the NGC 5253-B signal has not been associated with any known host structure. The pulse train was first noticed in archival data collected over the past two years and only identified after the team developed a new signal-processing pipeline designed to detect faint, periodic sources. A similar candidate signal reported by a different team in 2021 near the same galaxy was later attributed to a satellite pass and retracted; the authors note their detection pipeline specifically flags and removes known satellite trajectories, though they acknowledge no such filter is perfect.

Meridian Industrial Holdings — Annual Report Excerpt, Segment Review.

Meridian Industrial Holdings operates through three reportable segments: Meridian Fabrication, Coreline Logistics, and Aspen Materials, the latter acquired in March of the reporting year.

Meridian Fabrication, the company's largest segment, generated revenue of $1.24 billion, roughly flat compared to $1.21 billion in the prior year. Segment operating margin declined to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributes to higher steel input costs that were only partially offset by price increases passed to customers.

Coreline Logistics revenue grew 18% to $640 million, driven by increased freight volumes and a new long-term contract with a major grocery chain that began in the second quarter. This segment's operating margin improved to 9.8% from 8.1%.

Aspen Materials, acquired for $310 million in an all-cash transaction, contributed $95 million in revenue during its nine months of ownership within the reporting year; on a pro forma full-year basis, management estimates Aspen would have contributed approximately $130 million. Aspen's results are not included in prior-year comparatives, as the acquisition had not yet closed.

Risk Factors (excerpt): The company notes that Meridian Fabrication's profitability is sensitive to steel and aluminum commodity prices, which the company does not hedge beyond short-term supplier contracts. The company also discloses an ongoing dispute with a former Coreline Logistics customer over contract termination fees, seeking damages of approximately $8 million; the company believes the claim is without merit and intends to contest it, but notes that litigation outcomes are inherently uncertain and an adverse ruling could result in a charge to earnings.

Total company revenue across all segments, including corporate eliminations of $14 million, was $1.965 billion for the reporting year, compared to $1.85 billion in the prior year.

The company's board approved a share repurchase program of up to $150 million, though as of the report date no shares had yet been repurchased under the new authorization.

Liquidity: As of the end of the reporting year, the company held $210 million in cash and cash equivalents and had $180 million available under its revolving credit facility, which matures in three years. Total long-term debt was $580 million, with a weighted average interest rate of 5.4%.

Outlook: Management expects Meridian Fabrication's margin pressure to ease gradually in the coming year as recently negotiated steel supply contracts take effect, though it cautions that commodity prices remain volatile and that no specific margin target is being provided at this time.
